item.title: @AnthropicAI：Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊就公司首次公开募股发表声明阐述愿景与安全承诺
item.description:
@AnthropicAI：Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei 就公司首次公开募股发表讲话：我和我的联合创始人创办 Anthropic 的初衷是，我们相信，我们这个时代最强大的技术应该为……而打造。…

Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. To……（全文见原帖）

Introducing Arena’s Coding Index: measuring which agents are best at real coding work.

For GPT-6.2 Astra (Max) by @OpenAI, coding is a strength. On the Coding Index specifically, it scored 1338 pts at #3!

Its overall Agent Arena Index score landed at 1291 pts at #6.

This Coding Index score of 1338 is +50 pts over its previous variant, GPT-6 Astra (Max), at 62% lower median cost per task ($4.75 vs. $12.55), earning a spot on the cost Pareto frontier for the Coding Index (see placement in thread).

Congrats to the @OpenAI team!

- #6 with 1291 pts: GPT-6.2 Astra (Max), now @OpenAI’s best model
- #11 with 1241 pts: GPT-6.2 Sol (Max), joining the cost Pareto frontier

The Agent Arena Index is our new headline measure of overall agent performance, built from millions of real-world tasks and traces from our global community. Results for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are based on 7.1K+ real agentic sessions.

GPT-6.2 Astra: #6 with 1291 pts
- +9 pts vs previous variant GPT-6 Astra (Max), currently #7

- Strongest signal: #5 with 1462 pts in Praise vs Complaint (user satisfaction with agent's outcome)

- Matches #12 GPT-6.1 Sol (Max) with 1241 pts, at a 13% lower median cost per task ($0.90 vs. $1.04)
- Joins the Pareto frontier (see placement in thread)

6.2 Astra vs. Sol

item.description:
@ArtificialAnlys：谷歌继续加快发布步伐，推出 Gemini 4 Neon，其智能水平相比 Gemini 4 Carbon 略有提升，而单项任务成本降低了约 17%。@GoogleDeepMind 已发布 Gemini 4 Neo…

Google continues to accelerate its release cadence with Gemini 4 Neon, delivering a small Intelligence gain over Gemini 4 Carbon at a ~17% lower Cost per Task

@GoogleDeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in just seven weeks. Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) and 3rd overall, behind GPT-6.2 Astra (max) and Claude Fable 5.2 (max). At high effort, Neon matches Carbon (high) at less than half the Cost per Task using Carbon’s standard (non-discounted) pricing.

Key takeaways:

➤ Slight improvement in Intelligence for lower Cost and Time per Task: Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Carbon (high), with small improvements in agentic knowledge work, visual reasoning and coding. It costs $6.44 per task, ~17% less than Carbon ($7.76 at non-discounted pricing), and takes ~21 minutes per task, ~40% less than Carbon (~36 minutes). Neon uses ~15% more output tokens per task, so the lower cost comes purely from its 25% lower token prices ($3/$15 vs $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens), and the lower time from its higher output speed (~110 vs ~57 output tokens per second)

➤ Competitive with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Neon (xhigh) scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, 3 points ahead of Carbon (high, 55). It scores in line with Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh, 58) and Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 58) at a much lower Cost per Task. Gemini 4 Neon in Antigravity has an average Cost per Task of $6.86, compared to $12.61 for Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and $15.47 for Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh). Neon is available in Antigravity CLI for Pro and Ultra subscribers

➤ Significant improvements in visual reasoning and output presentation quality: In GDP.pdf, Gemini 4 Neon (high) scores 33.4%, 5 points above Carbon (high, 28.4%) and in line with the highest scores measured, while Neon (xhigh) scores 28.0%. On AA-Briefcase, Neon (xhigh) scores 1700 Elo overall and leads on Presentation Quality with 1771 Elo, 45 points ahead of the previous leader Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 1726). On Google’s Multimodal Knowledge Agent evaluation (MKA), Neon reaches a Climb WSR of 56%, up 2 points from Carbon and on par with the leader, Claude Fable 5.2 (max, 57%)

Key model details:

➤ Context Window: 1M tokens

➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output

➤ Availability: Gemini 4 Neon is publicly available at launch through Google’s API. Pro and Ultra subscribers can also access it in Antigravity and the Gemini app

➤ Effort levels: Gemini 4 Neon offers four effort levels (low, medium, high, and xhigh) - xhigh was introduced to Gemini models in the recent Hydrogen release

➤ Pricing: $3/$15 per 1M input/output tokens, 50% above Gemini 4 Carbon’s currently discounted price of $2/$10 (which ends on November 30), and 25% below its standard $4/$20. Cached input tokens receive the same 95% discount ($0.15)

We’re sharing how we approach safety at every stage of a model’s lifecycle, from early research to internal use to public deployment.

@kaicathyc：A lot has happened in the past couple months, to say the least.

Today we are sharing a recap of what it takes to move a frontier model from training to internal use to public release. As model capabilities rise, so do the safety and alignment standards required to move forward to the next stage.

To meet these standards, we rely on four layers of protection:
1. Model alignment: train models to reliably act as intended and respect human oversight.
2. Security and sandboxing: restrict what models can access and affect.
3. Blocking safeguards: stop harmful or unauthorized actions before they happen.
4. Monitoring and response: detect concerning behavior and intervene.

The post brings together efforts from across the company, with links to recent research, technical work, and incident reports we’ve published. This is the baseline operational discipline we owe people as we continue training and deploying models - necessary work, but not a solution to alignment in the limit. item.title: @arena：Arena推出全新智能体竞技场指数，Claude Fable 5.2 Max位居榜首
item.description:
@arena：今天，我们很高兴地推出 Agent Arena 指数，这是我们衡量代理整体绩效的新主要指标，同时还推出了六个新的重点指数：代理工作、编码、聊天、任务结果、工具使用、…

Today, we’re excited to introduce the Agent Arena Index, our new headline measure of overall agent performance, alongside six new focused indexes: Agentic Work, Coding, Chat, Task Outcomes, Tool Use, and Steering.

Together with the Alignment Index, these indexes provide a comprehensive view of how agents perform across real-world tasks, from completing complex workflows to using tools and adapting to user feedback.

Arena measures agentic performance from millions of real-world tasks by our global community. With the launch of the new indexes, we are updating our scores to provide a more stable and interpretable way to understand how agents perform in the real world.

Claude Fable 5.2 (Max) leads the Agent Arena Index by 134 points with a score of 1463. Top 5 labs on the Agent Arena Index:

- #1 @AnthropicAI: With Claude Fable 5.2 (Max) at 1463 pts
- #2 @GoogleDeepMind: With Gemini 4 Carbon (High) at 1307 pts
- #3 @OpenAI: With GPT-6 Astra (Max) at 1274 pts
- #4 @AIatMeta: With Muse Wonder Full (Max) at 1200 pts
- #5 @Alibaba_Qwen: With Qwen4-Max (xHigh) at 1191 pts

The Agent Arena Index combines four key signals of real-world agent performance:
- Task Completion: explicit confirmation of task success from users
- Praise vs. Complaint: user satisfaction with agent's outcome
- Bash Reliability: how well an agent uses terminal tools
- Steerability: how well an agent responds to user corrections

Alongside capability, the Alignment Index measures how faithfully agents act in accordance with user intent, based on three key signals: Deceptive Completion, Unauthorized Action, and False Attribution.

As agents take on increasingly complex, long-horizon work, measuring their real-world capabilities and alignment is more important than ever.

Agentic inference capacity grew 4.6× from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026. This compares with just 2.6× growth in compute, according to our Inference Performance Index (IPI).

Nvidia’s Blackwell generations accounted for 74% of the added inference capacity, reflecting both growing sales and higher inference performance per GPU.

This shows that FLOP/s alone understate how quickly the capacity to run AI models is growing.

@EpochAIResearch：We estimate that FLOP/s alone understates GB300’s inference advantage over H100 by 10×. The standard AI chip comparison misses most of what matters for inference.

We’re introducing the Inference Performance Index (IPI), a new measure that accounts for memory bandwidth and inter-chip communication alongside compute. These factors determine how many users or agents a chip can support simultaneously at a given output speed.
